history unlike caesar's crossing of the rubicon second in caesar's case we have lots of direct physical evidence we have a number of inscriptions and coins produced soon after the republican civil war the early church or by witnesses like peter or joseph of arimathea third for caesar we have unbiased corroboration even caesar's enemies like cicero reported the crossing of the rubicon as did other segments.text: a Pharisee who specifically explains that our current bodies are inevitably corruptible and must return to the earth from which they came; so God will give us new,

segments.speaker: Richard Carrier
segments.text: better bodies in the resurrection.

segments.speaker: Richard Carrier
segments.text: Philo,

segments.speaker: Richard Carrier
segments.text: another Jew,

segments.speaker: Richard Carrier
segments.text: and a contemporary of Paul,

segments.speaker: Richard Carrier
segments.text: also held to a similar view.

segments.speaker: Richard Carrier
segments.text: And Josephus and Philo often used the very same concepts and language as Paul.

segments.speaker: Richard Carrier
segments.text: Thus there is a good probability that Paul shared their view and understood the resurrection just as they did,

segments.speaker: Richard Carrier
segments.text: as an exchange of an old shell of a body for a new heavenly body.

segments.speaker: Richard Carrier
segments.text: This would explain one peculiar fact about the letters of Paul-why he never once mentions the empty tomb,

segments.speaker: Richard Carrier
segments.text: or any details of the empty tomb story.

segments.speaker: Richard Carrier
segments.text: Because the tomb wasn't empty; rather the corpse was empty.
